text_summary.body: Cyrus, stirred by the LORD to fulfil Jeremiah's word, proclaims in writing throughout his kingdom that the God of heaven has charged him to build a house at Jerusalem, and that any of his people may go up and build it, helped by their neighbours' gifts.

setting.body: The Cyrus Cylinder (Babylon, c. 539–530) records that Cyrus returned the images of gods to their sanctuaries and gathered and returned their inhabitants for cities across the Tigris and in Sumer and Akkad; it does not name Judah or Jerusalem.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V10B5RBQJP52A16XSXQW14
constraints.textual_assertion: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia
assumptions: "First year of Cyrus" counted as his first Babylonian year (24 Mar 538 – Mar 537); counting from his rule in Persia would be meaningless here, since the decree presupposes the conquest of Babylon.

competing_reconstructions.label: 538 BC (Cyrus's first Babylonian year)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Year 1 = 24 Mar 538 – Mar 537 on Nisan reckoning.

competing_reconstructions.label: Cyrus moved by Isaiah's prophecy (Josephus)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Josephus says Cyrus learned his charge "by his reading the book which Isaiah left behind"; no Persian source mentions it. The Cyrus Cylinder presents Marduk, not the LORD, as Cyrus's divine patron in Babylon.

competing_reconstructions.label: Cyrus's mission foretold in Isaiah (dating disputed)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Isa 44:28 and 45:13 announce the rebuilding and release that Ezra 1 records; whether the oracle predates Cyrus is disputed (claim under review).

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik dates the decree to 538, cites the Cyrus Cylinder (via Payne and Kidner) as confirming Cyrus's policy, and suggests Daniel may have shown Cyrus Isaiah 44:28–45:5.

open_questions: The Aramaic memorandum (Ezra 6:3–5) and the Hebrew proclamation (Ezra 1:2–4) differ in form; their relation was not researched.
